about: A Go library for reading, converting and writing subtitle files such as SRT and WebVTT.

prs.title: Subtitles keep the text after a blank line
prs.broken: When a subtitle in an SRT file had a blank line inside it, everything after that line was lost.
prs.changed: Removing empty lines at the end now stops at the last line with text, so the rest of the subtitle stays.
prs.matters: Players and tools that read SRT files show the whole subtitle.

prs.title: YouTube subtitles no longer lose the text of a cue
prs.broken: YouTube's auto-generated WebVTT files start each cue with a line holding one space. The reader took that line as the end of the cue, so the text after it was lost.
prs.changed: A line of only spaces before a cue's text is now skipped, while one after the text still ends the cue.
prs.matters: Converting YouTube captions keeps every line of text.

prs.title: WebVTT symbols survive a conversion
prs.broken: Reading WebVTT decoded only three HTML codes, so speaker-change marks and apostrophes in YouTube captions came out as raw codes after converting.
prs.changed: Cue text now decodes every standard HTML code.
prs.matters: Converted captions show the real characters instead of codes.

prs.title: Two-line subtitles stay on two lines in ASS files
prs.broken: The SSA and ASS writer used a soft line break, which players show as a space, so every two-line subtitle played on one line.
prs.changed: The writer now uses the hard line break.
prs.matters: Subtitles converted to ASS look the same in mpv, VLC and ffmpeg as in the source.

prs.title: Styled subtitle lines keep their spacing in SSA/ASS
prs.broken: Converting subtitles with italic or bold words to SSA/ASS added stray spaces, so "Hello world!" came out as "Hello  world !".
prs.changed: The pieces of a line are now joined as they are, the way the other formats already did.
prs.matters: Converted subtitles read normally instead of showing odd gaps around styled words.
